questions.question: Manufacturing alone contributes roughly what share of South Africa's GDP?
"A country that exports raw materials and imports finished goods sells cheap and buys dear" is the argument for:
options: Beneficiation — adding value locally before export

questions.question: Manufacturing's backward linkages connect it to:
options: The tertiary services that sell its goods
The primary sector it buys raw materials from

questions.question: South Africa's flagship manufactured export industry is:
options: Vehicles, from plants such as Rosslyn, Kariega, East London and Durban

subtopics.title: The Types of Industries: A Field Guide

questions.question: Iron and steel production at Vanderbijlpark is classified as:
Sugar mills locate in the KwaZulu-Natal cane belt because cane is:
options: Heavy, perishable and weight-losing in processing

questions.question: Breweries and bakeries are market-orientated because:
options: Their products are heavier, more fragile or more perishable than their inputs
Their raw materials cannot be transported

questions.question: A software firm choosing its location for skills, lifestyle and connectivity is an example of:
Aluminium smelters at Richards Bay illustrate location driven by:
The Vaal River system anchors Gauteng's heavy industry because such industry needs:
Special Economic Zones and Industrial Development Zones are examples of which location factor?
options: Political intervention steering industry with incentives and infrastructure

questions.question: In a location-scenario question, top marks go to answers that:
options: Weigh the factors and identify the two or three that dominate for that industry

questions.question: Load-shedding hinders industrial development by:
options: Halting production lines, spoiling batches and raising investor risk

questions.question: Over-concentration of industry means:
options: Too many products from one factory
Industry crowded into a few core regions, causing congestion there and starving other areas of investment
Factories built too close to mines

questions.question: The Vaal Triangle and Durban South basin are named in this topic as examples of:
"Evaluate South Africa as an industrial location" differs from "account for slow growth" because evaluation requires:
options: A map of the four regions
Both pans of the scale — hindrances AND strengths like the diversified base, capital markets and trade access

subtopics.title: Why the Factory Matters: The Sandwich Rule

questions.question: In the sandwich rule, the jump from raw tomato to bottled sauce represents:
The "sell-raw-buy-back trap" means a country that exports raw materials and imports finished goods:
options: Pays other countries' workers to make its money for it

questions.question: The "gears" behind one factory represent:
options: The machinery on the factory floor
Multiplier jobs — suppliers, transport and shops supported by the factory

subtopics.title: The Tuck-Shop Test: Where Does a Business Sit?

questions.question: The tuck-shop sits inside the school because:
options: Its customers cannot travel and its product must be fresh — market orientation

questions.question: The one-line version of the tuck-shop test is: the factory sits at the end that is:
options: Heavier, bulkier or more likely to spoil

questions.question: "Every town has its bakery and its brickworks" describes which industry type?
Factories camping "at the harbour gates" where cargo changes mode are:
options: Bridge industries — like Durban's port-side refining and assembly

subtopics.title: Choosing an Address, and What Makes It Hard

questions.question: "A smelter is basically electricity turned solid" argues that a smelter's dominant location factor is:
Weak rail freight hinders industry because:
options: Cargo shifts to costlier road transport and ports jam

questions.question: Over-concentration in one sentence:
options: Factories are too large to manage
Nearly everything crowds into four regions, choking them while the rest waits for investment
Each region has too many different industries

questions.question: The "two-handed conclusion" weighs the hindrance list against:
options: The size of neighbouring economies only
Africa's most complete industrial machine — diversified factories, banks, universities and trade access
The history of the gold mines
